fact_check_verdict: Abstract-level only (paper body 403). Say roughly 3x per the authors, never absolute counts. Not a claim about AEC. Do not claim long-run seismicity tripled.

claims.spoken: Two scientists built a machine-learning earthquake catalog for the Alaska Peninsula.
They are G. Barcheck of Cornell and N. A. Ruppert of the U S G S.
It was published online October twenty-eighth in Earth and Space Science.
The data come from a seafloor experiment in twenty eighteen and twenty nineteen.
That experiment put seismometers on land and on the seafloor.
It used 105 broadband seismometers, thirty on land and seventy-five on the ocean floor.
requires: From Barcheck et al 2020 SRL, the experiment description, not the 2026 paper.

claims.spoken: The array covered about seven hundred kilometers of the subduction zone, from Kodiak to the Shumagin Islands.
requires: Kodiak/Shumagin from FDSN network page XO_2018; 700 km from SRL abstract.

claims.spoken: Human analysts had already checked the earthquakes that experiment recorded.
The team used those human-checked picks to train a model called EQTransformer.
requires: EQTransformer is pre-existing (Mousavi et al 2020); authors fine-tuned it.

claims.spoken: EQTransformer is a deep-learning model that finds earthquakes and picks their arrivals in the same pass.
They tried several training strategies, and none was substantially better than the others.
requires: Strategies named in the abstract: choice of pre-trained starting model, addition of waveform bandpass filtering, and choice of random metadata split. Verbatim: 'We evaluate the effect of choice of pre-trained starting model, addition of waveform bandpass filtering, and choice of random metadata split.'

claims.spoken: What improved the model was simply local data to learn from.
requires: Word ban: avoid 'matters'. Verbatim: 'simply having a local waveform data set to fine-tune the picking model substantially improves performance'.

claims.spoken: Then they ran the model across the continuous recordings to find new small earthquakes.
The machine-learning catalog has roughly three times as many earthquakes as the analyst-checked catalog.
requires: Say 'roughly', 'according to the authors'. No absolute counts. Applies to this 2018-2019 catalog only.

claims.spoken: The smallest quake it reliably catches got smaller by one tenth to four tenths of a magnitude unit.
Detection improved most far offshore and in the outer rise.
claims.on_screen: BIGGEST GAINS · FAR OFFSHORE · OUTER RISE

claims.spoken: The outer rise is the bulge where the ocean plate bends before it dives.
claims.on_screen: OUTER RISE · PLATE BENDS BEFORE IT DIVES

claims.spoken: With the extra small quakes, the map of where earthquakes cluster still matches earlier observations.
requires: Word ban: 'patterns' is banned in spoken copy.

claims.spoken: In twenty twenty-one a magnitude eight point two earthquake struck near Chignik.
In nineteen thirty-eight the same stretch produced a magnitude eight point two earthquake near the Semidi Islands.
requires: USGS M8.23. Do not say 'same segment' without hedge.

claims.spoken: The authors list funding from the National Science Foundation and the U S G S.
The instruments ran from May 2018 through August 2019.
requires: From the 2020 AACSE SRL experiment abstract. Supports calling it a 2018 to 2019 experiment.
